(See AMC 23.321 (c))
(a) Flight load factors represent the ratio of the aerodynamic force component (acting normal to the assumed longitudinal axis of the aeroplane) to the weight of the aeroplane. A positive flight load factor is one in which the aerodynamic force acts upward, with respect to the aeroplane.
(b) Compliance with the flight load requirements of this subpart must be shown –
  (1) At each critical altitude within the range in which the aeroplane may be expected to operate;
  (2) At each weight from the design minimum weight to the design maximum weight; and
  (3) For each required altitude and weight, for any practicable distribution of disposable load within the operating limitations specified in CS 23.1583 to 23.1589.
(c) When significant the effects of compressibility must be taken into account.
